absoluteSnow2027RideNotes.evidence: Article covers Salomon's 2026/27 range and states its team rode the range. Ross is identified with the Assassin Pro and reports having fun when riding fast/pushing it, strong pop, a solid underfoot feel, and enough creativity for a go-to board. This is a short single-rider qualitative note. It does not disclose board length, number of sessions, exact dates, snow/surface conditions, rider profile, or a repeatable test protocol; do not infer numerical scores or universal performance.

backcountry2027RetailListing.evidence: Identifies the item as 2027, lists USD 699.95 and the same seven sizes, and contains an anonymous Gearhead description of smooth dampening in variable/chattery snow, control at speed, and confidence on larger landings. The page says 'Be the first to review'; it does not identify the tester, size, date, conditions in detail, or method. Treated as weak retailer qualitative corroboration only, not an independent review or scoring input. Its detailed size table is secondary and is not merged into the official size table below.

scoringReview.decision: Keep all six existing scores unchanged. Ross's brief 2026/27 ride note broadly corroborates solid support at speed, pop and freestyle creativity, but its absent sample size, conditions, rider details and method do not justify precise numeric recalibration. The Backcountry Gearhead note is anonymous retailer commentary and is not treated as an independent test. Stability/response/park are directionally plausible but low-confidence; float lacks direct snow-condition observations; forgiveness lacks controlled edge-catch/landing observations; value is especially low-confidence because no China-market price was verified. Do not map manufacturer design claims or retailer claims to numeric scores.
